channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Keeping FT governors is pure virtue signalling, claims chair
item.description: The chair of one of the country’s largest foundation trusts has dismissed pledges by other FTs to keep their councils of governors as “virtue signalling”.

item.title: Letby trust criticised over fetus storage
item.description: The trust where Lucy Letby worked has been heavily criticised for how it looks after the bodies of fetuses.

item.title: ICB orders all GPs to use ‘distrusted’ IT system
item.description: An integrated care board has ordered all of its 337 GP practices to use a single digital access system and is switching off five rival products to save money.

item.title: Revealed: ICBs where majority use private dentist
item.description: More people have access to a private dentist than an NHS one in nine integrated care board areas – mostly driven by poor NHS provision, according to new figures.

item.title: Hospitals given two months to put CCTV cameras in neonatal units
item.description: Trusts have been told to fit CCTV in neonatal units by the end of November and to “urgently” tell staff and boards that child death protocols cover babies who never leave hospital.

item.title: Regions ‘should penalise trusts for poor tech’
item.description: Advanced foundation trust status should be dependent on meeting digital maturity targets with “consequences” for non-compliance, an influential new report advises.

item.title: Flagship digital programme ‘a shambles’
item.description: Trust leaders have branded a national tech investment programme “a shambles” and questioned whether cash will be released before the end of its first year.

item.title: Alarm raised over impact of management cuts on NHS productivity
item.description: “Politically attractive” cuts to managers could harm the NHS’s productivity, a major NHS commission has warned.

item.title: Exclusive: Investigations launched into potential harm at children’s service
item.description: A major acute trust has launched two reviews over care failures potentially affecting 130 children, HSJ has learned.

item.title: We’re providing ‘pretty awful’ care, says CEO
item.description: A hospital trust is providing a “pretty awful” standard of care, its interim chief executive has declared.

item.title: Exclusive: National ‘neighbourhood’ director stepping down
item.description: The national lead for neighbourhood health and former national medical director has resigned, HSJ has learned.

item.title: Trust faces decade-long review after hundreds of harm cases discovered
item.description: More than 300 cases of patient harm have been identified at a North East trust reviewing major care and governance failings in its breast cancer service.

item.title: Ministers hire economist to scrutinise cancer performance
item.description: Health economist Anita Charlesworth will independently co-chair a “reformed” National Cancer Board, seven months after the government’s cancer plan promised a body “accountable for delivery” of its commitments.

item.title: Strategy director leaves NHSE
item.description: NHS England’s strategy director – a former special political adviser in the Treasury and health department – has left the role.

item.title: Tech problem delays elective reform target
item.description: Concerns have been raised about NHS England watering down a key target for its controversial “advice and guidance” scheme, just weeks ahead of the October deadline.

item.title: Board shake-up at ailing hospital group
item.description: The chair of a large hospital group has announced he will be stepping down after three years, amid a major board shake-up.

item.title: Judge to examine trust’s care failings
item.description: Government has named a chair for its public inquiry into care and governance failings at a mental health trust – nine months after the probe was promised.

item.title: GP leaders seek end to ‘hostilities’
item.description: The British Medical Association’s GP committee has voted against escalating its “collective action”, in a bid to “reset” its relationship with government and NHS England.

item.title: Six ‘neighbourhoods’ seek investors to ‘derisk’ expansion
item.description: Six “neighbourhood health” projects are being pump-primed by government to secure millions of pounds of private investment.

item.title: Private providers face tougher rules on payment
item.description: A major government review into the prevalence of mental illness and neurodivergence is set to call for a mandatory tariff and specification to tackle huge variation in price and quality in ADHD and autism services, HSJ understands.
